Dear Hiring Manager,

I'm applying for the Junior Data Analyst job you posted last week. I have a degree in statistics and I've spent the past year turning messy data into recommendations people actually used, so this role looks like a good fit.

During my internship at a regional distribution company, I analyzed delivery records to figure out why shipments were late. I cleaned and merged data from three sources in SQL and Excel (the carrier data was a mess), then built a Tableau dashboard that tracked on-time performance by route and carrier. Operations used it in their Monday meetings, and after they changed two problem routes, delays dropped by 12 percent the next quarter.

For my capstone I forecast warehouse demand with Python, pandas and scikit-learn. I presented it to faculty and a couple of people from industry, and honestly the presenting taught me more than the model did: explaining results in plain language is half the job.

I like logistics because small changes in routing or inventory show up quickly in cost and in how happy customers are. Your company seems to take data seriously, which is where I want to start.

Thanks for your time. I'm happy to send work samples or references.

Sincerely,
Sam Ortega
